transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I… I’m having trouble when I drive toward Miami, over those long bridges. As soon as my car gets on one, my chest tightens and I grip the wheel, and I feel like I have to get off right away… even though there isn’t anywhere to go.
Do you get this same fear only on bridges?
Mostly, yes… it’s really the bridges over all that water. I know they’re safe, I know people drive them every day, but in my mind it feels… much more dangerous than it probably is.
When this happens on a bridge, is your main fear that the bridge itself is dangerous?

Not exactly that it’s going to fall down. I know those bridges have been there a long time, and people cross them every day. It’s more… being out over all that open water. The fear just feels much bigger than the real danger, I suppose.
If you were on a boat out on open water, would you feel that same fear?
I think… yes, probably. It’s the open water that gets to me. I know it isn’t really as dangerous as it feels, but my mind doesn’t seem to accept that in the moment.
Have you ever had one of these attacks come on suddenly when you were not near open water?
I don’t think so… not that I can recall. It seems tied to being near that kind of water.
